newsitem.title: TURKEY: Afghan Dostum says he wants peace with rival.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Dostum says he wants peace with rival.

text.p: Exiled Afghan warlord Abdul Rashid Dostum said on Thursday he wanted to make peace with a former comrade who ousted him in a mutiny last week, allowing the Islamic Taleban militia to take over a key northern town.
"I want to make peace with General Abdul Malik," Turkey's state-run Anatolian news agency quoted Dostum as saying.
Dostum said he wanted Ankara to mediate between him and Abdul Malik, whose forces took over the Dostum stronghold town of Mazar-i-Sharif in alliance with the Taleban last weekend.
Dostum, an ethnic Uzbek, fled to Turkey after his ouster. He has holed up in an Ankara hotel since May 24.
Abdul Malik, formerly a commander in Dostum's ethnic Uzbek forces, later turned on the Taleban and chased them out of Mazar-i-Sharif in fierce fighting that ended on Wednesday.
Turkey said on Monday that Dostum could stay in the country as long as he wanted. Turks and Uzbeks share ethnic and linguistic links.
